Extract Implicate-Level Estimates from SCF Summary Objects

Source: R/scf_implicates.R
scf_implicates.Rd

Retrieves implicate-level point estimates and (optionally) diagnostic statistics from SCF result objects returned by functions like scf_mean(), scf_freq(), or scf_xtab(). This is primarily a diagnostic tool that allows users to inspect variation across implicates before Rubin-style pooling is applied.

scf_implicates(x, metrics = TRUE)

Arguments

x

An object returned by an scf_ summary function (e.g., scf_mean, scf_freq) that contains an "implicates" attribute storing estimates for each of the five imputations.

metrics

Logical. If TRUE (default), the function attempts to extract not only point estimates but also standard errors, confidence intervals, and coefficients of variation. If FALSE, returns raw values only.

Value

If metrics = TRUE and diagnostics are available, returns:

  • A single data.frame of estimates if the summary is ungrouped

  • A list of data.frames (one per implicate) if the original summary was grouped

If metrics = FALSE, returns raw numeric values or implicate-level data as stored in the object.

Use Cases

This function is helpful for:

  • Inspecting variation across implicates

  • Understanding imputation-based uncertainty

  • Debugging pooled estimates that appear unstable or inconsistent

It is particularly useful for SCF analysts seeking transparency in the model-pooling process, or for developing sensitivity checks.

Methodology

For supported objects (e.g., lists of svystat or svystat.by), the function extracts:

  • estimate: point estimate for each implicate

  • se: standard error

  • lower, upper: 95% confidence interval

  • cv: coefficient of variation

These are returned per implicate to facilitate visual or numerical inspection. If the object stores raw values or lacks metric structure, they are returned directly.

See also

scf_mean(), scf_freq(), scf_xtab(), scf_MIcombine()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
result <- scf_mean(scf2022, ~networth)
scf_implicates(result)

grouped <- scf_mean(scf2022, ~networth, by = ~racecl)
scf_implicates(grouped)
} # }
